examples.description: Trace this package's fixtures and gate the committed reports against them. Named `examples` rather than `callidescope` so every examples package in this workspace runs the same way, and so it is never confused with `codebase:callidescope`, which is its mirror image: that target only ever publishes, because a report there goes stale on nearly every change and depth is gated by each project's own inferred `callidescope-gate` instead, while the fixtures traced here are frozen, so a stale report means a fixture, the resolver, or one of the three dependency packages this run's closure reaches moved — which is exactly the regression this package exists to catch. Those three packages' sources are named in `inputs` alongside the toolchain, because the closure measures them and their callables reach the committed reports, so a cached result is never replayed over a change to them. Their READMEs are not named, because this run publishes a `## 🔭 Callidescope` section only for the project it is scoped to. `{projectRoot}/examples/*/README.md` is named for the opposite reason: `gated-leaf` is a nested project this run is scoped to as well, so it carries that same section in its own guide, and `{projectRoot}/README.md` alone never reaches it — a hand-edit inside those anchors would otherwise replay a cached green over exactly the drift `--check reports` exists to catch. `{workspaceRoot}/configuration/*.config.ts` is named for a different reason and is not redundant with `shared-globals`, which holds `configuration/tsconfig.json` and nothing else: two of those three packages are in the closure only because this package's own `eslint.config.ts` and `codometer.config.ts` spread the root ones, and the root ones import `@codebase/logging/eslint` and `@codometer/configuration`. Drop an import there and the committed reports lose a whole project while every other input is untouched, so a cached green replays over exactly the drift `--check reports` exists to catch. The glob rather than those three files by name, because a closure is whatever the compiler read and a hand-written list of it goes stale in silence — which is the failure this input exists to prevent. It is a per-target input and never belongs in `shared-globals`, where a high-churn glob once cost the whole workspace every cache hit it had. Depth is not gated here at all: the deep fixtures are meant to breach, which is why `configuration/.callidescopeignore` keeps them out of the workspace run.
